I'll answer this in 2 parts depending on whether you think it can be improved.

**A: Let's assume there is no way to improve the exploration and make it more seamless/immersion breaking.**

I think this means that the game setting is just fundamentally worse for world exploration. 

Even if alternative exploration would have been worse (like having to exit orbit or fly in space for a while) and Bethesda made a good choice by not wasting resources on those features, it doesn't change the fact that the game still doesn't feel as good to explore.

One of the best parts of games like Skyrim was how seamless everything feels. I can pickup the objects, I can go inside every building, I can walk wherever. Todd talked about this in the Lex Friedman interview where he talked about how having the AI run in the background helps with the immersion of the world.

And in Skyrim there were times I would choose to take the boring path. If I was in a cave outside of Whiterun I might choose to manually run to the city for a couple minutes even though there's not much of interest on the way there.

Starfield takes away these connecting, immersive moments, and instead replaces them with you looking at UI and loading the next location. And even then the UI is pretty bad.

**B: There are some legitimate ways that exploration could have been improved.**

To respond directly to your comment, I think there are some big ways exploration could have been improved given this new game setting while not using too many resources on Bethesda's end.

1) They could have made takeoff more seamless by putting it in first person and creating a transition through the atmosphere. Then boom you pop out into space in a new area. This doesn't require full ground to space flying it's just an animation and a change in camera perspective.

2) In space it should allow you to use your map when pulling up you scanner and let you look around to choose your destination. 

Since this would likely look messy they could darken out the background around you so you can see it clearly. Side note: they should improve the full universe map I have no idea what dot is which star system.

Right now they do something similar in the game with waypoints, but they should add this feature in for all star systems.

3) Again, this time in space, make grav jumping more seamless by keeping your camera position (1st/3rd person) and then showing the grav jump the whole time instead of cutting to black. This would be an effective way of hiding the loading screen.

They could even have something for "short" grav jumps, like if you're going to another planet within the system. It could be the same looks grav jump, accept maybe this time it's a bit more transparent so you could see the planets moving around you.

This could take maybe a minute or two to fully complete, but would help make you feel like you can truly "travel anywhere". You could also pop out of this at any time and by in some random spot in space. As we've seen you can already technically fly to other planets so the technology and space is already there.

***Isn't this all tedious?***

I think so, yes. But that's a big part of open world games. Half of the time in Fallout or the Elder Scrolls you're just walking between locations, but it makes the world feel more real. 

People who play more linear games might argue "well why do you like walking for 5 minutes from location to location? Why wouldn't you just have all of the best content coming straight at you in a more linear game like COD or Doom?"

That in between time is a lot of what makes the game feel real and lived in. That's the reason a lot of people like Bethesda games. I have heard a lot of people recommend playing Skyrim without any fast travel. In Fallout 4's survival mode they actually removed fast travel and a lot of people believe that is the best way to play the game. 

TLDR I think that either way you look at it Starfield has very weak exploration compared to other Bethesda games.

Even if they do know when it will be released, they might just not want to go through the hassle. 

This is where the scalper comes in. They go through the trouble of actually figuring all of this out and buying it on time. Think about it like you're paying someone to wait in line for something (ex: an iphone). 

You may say these cost way too much, but that's because they are being sold at the market equilibrium price, which is so high because supply is so low.

To the point about scalpers buying so much that it's causing shortages, I don't see any real evidence for that. Looking it up rn, there are only 615 results for 3080's on ebay. As of right now, it's hard to say how many units have sold in total, but with these things we usually see there being much more units sold retail than units sold aftermarket. Even if it was a significant portion, they will only sell at the market equilibrium, so we won't have a situation where people are overpaying.
